subject: physics_2
question_text: Among alpha, beta and gamma radiation which get affected by the electric field?

mark_split.label: Alpha and beta deflect — they are charged
Gamma does not — it has no charge

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: α carries +2e, β carries −e (β⁺ carries +e), so an electric field deflects both; γ is electromagnetic radiation with no charge and is not deflected. The book's printed answer names only alpha and beta; the gamma statement completes the comparison the question asks for.

recall_prompt: Say which radiations an electric field deflects, and why the third one is not deflected.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Alpha and beta are deflected
lines: Alpha and beta radiation are deflected by an
electric field, because they carry charge.
An α-particle carries +2e and a β-particle
steps.margin_note: First mark. Name both radiations and give the reason: they are charged.
steps.why: An electric field exerts force F = qE only on charge. Naming the charges (+2e and −e) shows the reason, not just the fact.
common_mistakes: Saying only alpha is deflected. Beta is charged too and deflects the opposite way.
Giving the fact without the reason. The charge is what earns the mark.

recall.must_convey: That alpha and beta are deflected because they carry charge.
accept: alpha is plus two e, beta is minus e
the field pulls on their charge

steps.memory_tip: Force needs charge: F = qE. Alpha and beta have q; that is the whole reason.

steps.label: Gamma is not deflected
lines: Gamma rays carry no charge — they are

lines.text: Alpha and beta deflect; gamma does not

steps.margin_note: Second mark. The question lists three radiations — account for gamma too.
steps.why: The question names all three radiations, so a complete answer must say what happens to gamma and why: no charge, no electric force.
common_mistakes: Leaving gamma out entirely. The question asks about all three.
Calling gamma a particle with a small charge. It is uncharged electromagnetic radiation.

recall.must_convey: That gamma carries no charge, so the field does not deflect it.

steps.memory_tip: Two of the three carry charge. Gamma does not — it is electromagnetic radiation, so it goes straight.

insider_note: Answer for all three radiations — the second mark is for saying gamma is NOT deflected and why, which the book's own printed answer skips.
